title: restore-deterministic-retries-and-structured-error-mapping-for-tool-calls
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes:
- Normalize Retry-After parsing (seconds or HTTP-date) for OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- Add `retryable` boolean to error payload to make retry behavior deterministic for clients
- Clarify idempotency ownership rules for tool/function calls in streaming sessions
- Improve error mapping so 429/503/502 are consistently classified across streaming and unary APIs
description:
Motivation: We have seen multiple customer incidents where clients retried aggressively after stream-level failures (partial stream disconnects, intermittent 502/503) or mis-parsed Retry-After (HTTP-date vs seconds). Tool/function calling flows add complexity: who owns idempotency (client vs server) across stream reconnects was ambiguous, leading to duplicate tool side-effects for some customers. This PR standardizes semantics across OpenAI-compatible endpoints and makes retry decisions deterministic for clients.

Summary of changes and behavior: - Normalize Retry-After header parsing to accept both integer seconds and HTTP-date; we expose a canonical `retry_after_seconds` field in the OpenAI-compatible error envelope for clients that prefer structured values. - Introduce a top-level `retryable` boolean in the OpenAI error object (same envelope used for streaming and non-streaming) to indicate whether a safe automated retry is recommended by the server. This decouples transport-level heuristics from client policy. - Define idempotency ownership rules for tool/function calls: the client-provided idempotency key (Idempotency-Key header or `idempotency_key` field) remains the canonical owner for deduplication across retries and reconnects; the server will reject ambiguous reconnects when ownership cannot be established. - Stream reconnection contract: when a streaming connection drops mid-response and the server returns an error with `retryable: true`, clients SHOULD resume by issuing a new request with the same idempotency key and start_position token (if server supports prefix resumption); otherwise they MUST treat the call as opaque and follow normal idempotency semantics. - Error mapping: map transient infra errors (502/503, connection reset, server overload) to OpenAI-style 500/429/503 error objects consistently and set `retryable` appropriately. - Backwards compatibility: existing clients that ignore `retryable` will continue to operate; new structured fields are additive.

Checklist: - [x] Normalize Retry-After parsing and add structured field - [x] Add `retryable` flag to error envelope - [x] Implement idempotency ownership checks in call routing - [x] Update OpenAI adapter tests for streaming reconnection scenarios - [x] Add docs and migration notes in docs/openai_compat/error_handling.md

Commits (high level): - a12b9c7: add structured retry_after_seconds and retryable boolean to openai error envelope - f3d4e1a: normalize Retry-After parsing across proxy + sdk shims - 9f7c4d5: enforce idempotency-key ownership for function/tool calls in router - 2b5a8f2: streaming reconnection support and tests for prefix resumption - 4e90d2b: docs and example client snippet + changelog entry

Changed areas (high level): - src/proxy/openai_adapter/error_envelope.go: add `RetryAfterSeconds` and `Retryable` fields and mapping helpers - src/proxy/openai_adapter/handlers.go: map transport errors to envelope consistently - src/runtime/streaming/resume.go: add prefix resumption hooks and ownership checks - src/runtime/idempotency/store.go: add strict ownership checks and TTL semantics - docs/openai_compat/error_handling.md: document the new contract and migration guidance - tests/openai_compat/stream_reconnect_test.go: new integration tests for reconnection + idempotency - examples/openai_compat/client_retry_example.md: example showing how to use the fields - ci/config: update integration matrix to include streaming reconnect tests

Small snippet (illustrative, single-line for copy/paste): `{"error": {"message": "server overloaded", "type": "rate_limit_exceeded", "retryable": true, "retry_after_seconds": 30}}`

Notes for reviewers: - The primary behavioral change is exposing `retryable` and the canonical `retry_after_seconds`. We intentionally keep HTTP Retry-After intact to preserve proxies and intermediate cache behavior; the structured field is for clients that want deterministic parsing. - Idempotency ownership is conservative: if a reconnect cannot be tied to the original idempotency key (missing header or mismatch), we return 409/422 with guidance rather than guessing. This reduces accidental duplicate tool invocation. - This surfaced a race in a small subset of routing tests; I fixed the router locks and added a dedicated integration test for concurrent reconnects.

Migration guidance (single-paragraph): Clients should start reading the `retryable` boolean and `retry_after_seconds` on OpenAI-compatible error payloads. For streaming function/tool calls, clients that want automatic transparent retries should supply a stable idempotency key for the lifetime of the logical operation and support prefix resumption tokens if they want to avoid restarting from scratch. Existing clients will continue to function but may be less deterministic in retry behavior.

CI and performance: Integration tests exercise high-concurrency streaming reconnection patterns. Local benchmarks show <2% regression in median latency for streaming start (the path touched a small lock in the router which I optimized).

Merge notes: Squash-merged to main after CI green and final approval from Maya and Liam.
